clue.text: Mentioned fish carried in the sack

indicators.note: whatever is carried in something sits inside it, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: to hit the sack is to go to bed, so the sack is slang for bed
a roach is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Someone reports a fish being hauled along in a sack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carried in the sack' paints a fisherman's bag, but the sack is slang for bed, as in 'hit the sack', and the fish sits inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To broach a subject is to raise it in conversation, so a topic brought up has been mentioned.

clue.text: 3 Down cold – extremely so!

definitions.note: 'so' stands for the 'cold' just before it, so the definition means extremely cold

blocks.note: 3 Down is curry, and a balti is a kind of curry
C is the abbreviation for cold on a tap

explanation.surface: A curry served cold, and very cold at that.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cold' does double duty: it gives C and is what 'so' points back to. A balti is a curry cooked in a wok-like pan, popular in Birmingham.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang Baltic describes freezing weather, named after the chilly northern sea, so it means very cold indeed.

clue.text: Work with jerks in light science

blocks.note: OP is short for opus, a work
tics are involuntary jerks or twitches

explanation.surface: Someone doing physics experiments with twitchy colleagues in a lab about light.
explanation.walkthrough: OP for a musical work is a standard abbreviation of opus.
explanation.definitionFit: Optics is the branch of physics studying the behaviour of visible radiation and lenses.

clue.text: Wild Ryder Cup row, it brings heat to course

indicators.note: something wild is unruly and out of order, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: An angry dispute at the Ryder Cup golf match heats up the course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Course' looks like the golf course from the Ryder Cup, but it is a course of a meal. The Ryder Cup is a golf contest between Europe and the USA.
explanation.definitionFit: Spice blend added to a dish, the meal course, gives it fiery flavour, which is the job of this seasoning.

clue.text: Last unopened message about your setter

indicators.note: something unopened has not had its front broken into, so the first letter is lost

blocks.note: a text message with its opening letter taken away
re means about or concerning
the setter refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: A final message left unread, concerning the person who wrote this puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last' looks like an adjective for the message, but it is the definition; setters often call themselves 'me' via phrases like 'your setter'.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme can mean furthest or final, as in the extreme end of a row, matching last.

clue.text: See 3
Boil bag – ordered to in part that must be played

indicators.note: to be ordered is to be put into a fresh sequence, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Cooking instructions: a boil-in-the-bag meal, ordered for the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash makes 'ordered' read as a cooking instruction, but it rearranges the letters before it.
explanation.definitionFit: In music an obbligato is an accompanying instrumental line that is essential and cannot be omitted, from the Italian for obligatory.

clue.text: Fearing day with lesson

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for day
a reading is a lesson, as read aloud in church

explanation.surface: A pupil anxious about a day with a lesson in it.
explanation.walkthrough: In church the lesson is the passage of scripture read out, which is why it can be a reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreading something means anticipating it with great apprehension, a near synonym of fearing.

clue.text: Liberated grass-covered meadows

indicators.note: a covered thing has something wrapped over it, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: a reed is a tall grass
leas are meadows, a poetic word

explanation.surface: Fields that have been freed and allowed to grow over with grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass-covered' reads as one adjective, but it says the grass covers the meadows: RE(LEAS)ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Released and liberated are synonyms, both meaning set free from confinement or restraint.

clue.text: Able to read temperature in boiling atelier

indicators.note: to be in something is to sit inside it, so one piece goes within another
boiling liquid churns about, so the letters are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for temperature
the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Checking the temperature reading in an overheated artist's studio.
explanation.walkthrough: An atelier is an artist's workshop; its rearranged letters take T inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: A literate person has learned reading and writing skills, so is capable of reading.

clue.text: Sailors with tale about halting descent

indicators.note: about can mean turned around, as in about-face, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: ABs are able seamen, ordinary sailors
a tale can be a fib or lie

explanation.surface: Sailors telling stories about stopping their ship's downward plunge.
explanation.walkthrough: AB, an able-bodied seaman, is the usual crossword sailor; LIE turned round follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: Abseiling is going down a cliff on a rope in a controlled, stop-start way, a descent made in stages.

clue.text: Old husband deserting this regretful socialite

indicators.note: deserting means leaving, so one letter departs from the word it was in

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
H is the abbreviation for husband
taken as written, losing the H

explanation.surface: An elderly husband walks out on a society lady who now has regrets.
explanation.walkthrough: O then THIS without its H gives O + TIS. Miss Otis Regrets is a Cole Porter song about a society lady who apologises she cannot come to lunch.
explanation.definitionFit: The heroine of Cole Porter's song sends word that she regrets being unable to lunch, making her the famous society lady with regrets.

clue.text: Wish to travel – minimal cost when cycling

indicators.note: cycling goes round and round, so a letter moves from one end to the other

blocks.note: titchy is British informal for very small
a fee is a charge or cost

explanation.surface: A traveller's dream: going places as cheaply as possible on a bicycle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cycling' looks like riding a bike, but it moves the first T of TITCHYFEE to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Having itchy feet is an idiom for restlessness and a longing to go somewhere new.

clue.text: Whence 3 Down cases of Hindu bias dismissed

indicators.note: the cases of something are its outer edges, which are the letters in question
dismissed means sent away, so the outer letters go and the insides remain

blocks.note: the word with its first and last letters removed
the word with its first and last letters removed

explanation.surface: A legal hearing: allegations of anti-Hindu prejudice thrown out of court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cases dismissed' sounds like a court report, but it strips the outsides off both words.
explanation.definitionFit: Curry, the 3 Down answer, originated in the cuisine of the Indian subcontinent, so whence means its country of origin.

clue.text: Hook’s first mate brings me empty boxes

indicators.note: a box holds things inside it, so the phrase contains the letters wanted

blocks.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: A pirate's assistant hands over a pile of empty crates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxes' looks like the cargo, but it is the verb: the phrase boxes the answer, brings ME Empty.
explanation.definitionFit: In Peter Pan, Smee is the bosun and loyal right-hand man of the villainous Captain Hook.

clue.text: Chap touring city in reverse, lawyer notes

indicators.note: going in reverse means travelling backwards, so the word runs the other way
touring a place means going all round it, so one piece surrounds another

blocks.note: a chap is a man
Rome is the Italian capital city
a DA is a district attorney, an American lawyer

explanation.surface: A man going round a city backwards while his lawyer takes notes.
explanation.walkthrough: The city is turned round before the chap goes round it; DA, district attorney, is an American prosecutor, a common crossword lawyer.
explanation.definitionFit: Memoranda is the Latin plural of memorandum, a written note or record for reminding.

clue.text: Playwright once called an Algonquian speaker

blocks.note: George Bernard Shaw, the Irish dramatist
née marks a woman's former surname, what she was once called

explanation.surface: A dramatist who used to go by a different name, introduced as a native speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: Née, French for born, introduces a maiden name, which is what someone was once called.
explanation.definitionFit: The Shawnee are a Native American people whose language belongs to the Algonquian family.

clue.text: Extra pages put in madden Dumas

indicators.note: something put in a phrase is lodged inside it, so the letters wanted sit within

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Extra pages inserted into a novel would infuriate the author Alexandre Dumas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put in' looks like inserting the pages, but it signals the answer is in the phrase, mADDEN DUMas.
explanation.definitionFit: An addendum is material added at the end of a book or document, often a few supplementary leaves.

clue.text: Didn’t see crashes en route

indicators.note: a crash smashes things up, so the letters are wrecked into a new order

blocks.note: the letters taken as written, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A driver who failed to look and so has accidents along the way.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as an excuse for a road accident; 'crashes' is the verb rearranging the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A traveller destined for a place is bound for it, already on the journey there.

clue.text: One imagines deer and ram cavorting

indicators.note: cavorting animals leap about wildly, so the letters jump into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone picturing a deer and a ram frolicking together in a field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One imagines' looks like the start of a sentence, but it is the definition: a person who imagines.
explanation.definitionFit: A dreamer is someone given to fantasies and visions, a person whose mind conjures things up.

clue.text: Fortieth anniversary gift is 3 Down for Cockneys

blocks.note: first meaning: the gemstone traditional for forty years of marriage
second meaning: Cockney rhyming slang for curry

explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang swaps a word for a phrase that rhymes and then drops the rhyme: Ruby Murray, a 1950s singer, rhymes with curry.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruby weddings mark four decades of marriage, and in East London slang going for a ruby means going for a curry.

clue.text: See 27
Tied house Diana missed in phone book

indicators.note: something missed is left out, so those letters are dropped from the word

blocks.note: Di is the short form of Diana
a telephone directory lists numbers

explanation.surface: Diana's pub listing has been left out of the telephone directory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tied house' looks like a brewery-owned pub, but here it is housing tied to a job. DIRECTORY loses DI.
explanation.definitionFit: A rectory is the home provided for a parish priest for as long as he holds the post, so it is tied to the job.

clue.text: Spice mix used in 3 Down, and in taramasalata!

indicators.note: in says the wanted letters lie inside the word that follows

blocks.note: the letters sit in the middle of the dip's name

explanation.surface: A spice blend found in curries, and surprisingly in a Greek fish-roe dip too.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark acknowledges the joke: taramasalata is a Greek dip, but the spice blend is there in its spelling, taraMASALAta.
explanation.definitionFit: Garam masala and other masalas are blends of ground spices, a staple of Indian cooking.

clue.text: Let It Be holds record for group

indicators.note: to hold something is to grip it within, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: stet, Latin for 'let it stand', is a proofreader's instruction to keep a deletion
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: The Beatles' album Let It Be holds a record for a band.
explanation.walkthrough: Let It Be looks like the Beatles song or album, but it is the instruction STET: S(EP)TET.
explanation.definitionFit: A septet is a set of seven, especially seven musicians playing together, a kind of musical group.

clue.text: Son exits holy festival: one in 3 Down house perhaps

indicators.note: to exit is to leave, so a letter departs from the word

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
Easter is the Christian festival of the resurrection

explanation.surface: A son leaves the Easter celebrations for an Indian restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: EASTER without its S. A curry house is British for an Indian restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: Diners in a curry restaurant are people having a meal there; 'perhaps' flags that a restaurant is just one example of where you find them.

clue.text: Performers’ private parts?

blocks.note: surface reading: an actor's intimate anatomy
setter's reading: the areas of a theatre closed to the audience and reserved for the cast

explanation.walkthrough: The cheeky surface points at anatomy; the question mark warns that 'parts' are areas of a building.
explanation.definitionFit: The region behind the theatre stage, with dressing rooms and wings, is off limits to the public and used by the cast.

clue.text: French composer‘s link with Pretoria?

blocks.note: Pretoria is a capital of South Africa, abbreviated SA
a tie is a link or connection

explanation.surface: Asking whether a French composer had some connection with the South African capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the indirect step from a city to its country, SA, and the order of pieces is the reverse of the clue's.
explanation.definitionFit: Erik Satie was a French composer famous for the Gymnopédies piano pieces.

clue.text: Uproar at home – 3 Down in place of roast?

blocks.note: a din is a loud uproar
someone at home is in
3 Down is curry, and to curry a horse is to groom it with a comb

explanation.surface: A household row breaks out when curry is served instead of the Sunday roast.
explanation.walkthrough: Curry here is the verb for brushing a horse, not the dish, so it gives GROOM.
explanation.definitionFit: The room where a family sits down to eat is where the Sunday joint is served; the question mark marks this as an example.

clue.text: Picture wine and endless dish served with 3 Down

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is cut off

blocks.note: port is a fortified wine
raita, a yogurt side dish eaten with curry, loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Imagine wine and a side dish with no end served alongside a curry.
explanation.walkthrough: Raita is a cooling dish of yogurt and cucumber served with curries; drop its final A.
explanation.definitionFit: A portrait is a painting or photograph of a person, a kind of picture.

clue.text: American doctor tucking into mum’s 3 Down

indicators.note: to tuck into something is to push inside it, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: Ma is mum, and the 's comes along
A is the abbreviation for American
DR is the abbreviation for doctor

explanation.surface: An American doctor eating his mother's homemade curry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tucking into' suggests eating, but here it means inserting; the 's of mum's is kept as letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A madras is a fairly hot curry named after the Indian city now called Chennai, so it is one kind of 3 Down.

clue.text: Actors following characters only given limited roles

indicators.note: one thing following another comes after it, so this piece goes second

blocks.note: type means printed characters or letters
the cast is the actors in a production

explanation.surface: Actors who play the same characters are stuck with narrow parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Characters' looks theatrical but means letters of print, TYPE.
explanation.definitionFit: A typecast actor keeps being chosen for the same kind of part, so their range of work is narrow.
